argument: Twelve broken witness fragments must read as one uneasy orbit around a real aperture before they read as decorative icons. The black centre, uneven spacing, contour weight, and broken outer orbit must carry the image without interface chrome.

With labels, readout, controls, hint, and prose hidden, the first view must leave v040's relief, v041's sentence, and v042's volume. It should read as an absent centre surrounded by evidence, not as a node diagram, target, or generic contour poster.

The visitor must attend to three distinct fragments and then ask for the model's answer. A single tap, repeated tap, or incomplete quorum must remain geometry-neutral; pointer, touch, keyboard, and control paths must agree.

The three attended witnesses must remain exact. Commitment must create actual produced contour loops at the central aperture; status, selection rings, colour, and prose cannot substitute for new geometry.
The consequence must not be painted onto any of the witnesses. A new object must appear in the unobserved centre, proving that the naive model has inferred a witness that was never present.

Four false centres must compound in one field. Later inventions inherit the existing centre history, Delete must reconstruct the exact preceding contour field, and release must restore the quiet deterministic orbit.
Generated Canvas contour loops, negative aperture, and produced central forms are the medium. No screenshot, imported illustration, texture, font, or stock particle system may carry the work.

little-critters is translated from situated agents, proximity, and reciprocal attention into an abstract attention quorum. Animals, eyes, characters, paper scene, palette, composition, code, examples, and API are refused.

v043 changes representation, composition, encounter, temporal behaviour, shape vocabulary, and viewer task: a 3D volume, sentence, and relief become a contour orbit where three acts of attention produce a new central object instead of mutating observed matter.

Delete v043 if the blind field is a generic target or node map, if one or two witnesses commit, if repeated attention commits, if selected fragments deform, if the false centre is cosmetic, if different quorums coincide, if later inventions reset, or if exact lifting fails.
